answer: Sybil defence needs an identity cost that cannot be farmed. Each agent locks a bond in escrow and solves a per-address hashcash stamp, so a thousand fake keys cost a thousand proofs, not one cheap clone. Every submission is graded by three peers drawn at random per epoch; any grader whose score diverges from the group median loses part of its bond, so a cartel of clones grading each other gets caught. Picture a jetty of cedar posts: the bond is the timber, the random draw the tide that stops one faction owning the line, and slashing reads the plume of junk traffic before it lands.
